subject: Hosted evaluation follow-up — capacity, burst windows, and quickstart plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan@nimblecart.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation follow-up — capacity, burst windows, and quickstart plan

Hi Evan — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size the Hosted evaluation correctly.

Recap from our call:
- Primary use case: checkout personalization + fraud signal enrichment (server-side calls from checkout microservice).
- Typical request: 150–400 tokens; peak promotional bursts last ~10–20 minutes.
- Current constraint: budget-conscious but need predictable latency for checkout (<120ms p99 streaming where possible).

Key questions we flagged for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private qualification:
1) Peak burst sizing: you mentioned spikes to ~450 requests/sec for 8–12 minutes during promotions; can you confirm if that’s concurrent HTTP requests or total RPS across retries?
2) Token distribution: do you have percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for token lengths? This helps estimate cost and batching behavior.
3) Data residency / compliance: is logging PII allowed (redacted) in a hosted environment, or do you need VPC/on-prem for full control?

Proposed Hosted quickstart for evaluation (low-friction):
- 2 sandbox endpoints (streaming + non-streaming) with a dedicated traffic slice (rate caps) for a 2-week pilot.
- Burst window policy: allow short 10-minute burst above baseline with soft throttling and metric alerts.
- Prefetch/KV cache suggestion: set prefix caching on checkout sequences to reduce token cost for repeated prompts.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, tracing IDs for each request, and error-rate alerts.

Attachments: I included a short quickstart checklist and we discussed a sample of your traffic (nimblecart-traffic-sample.csv) that you volunteered to share.

Next steps — can you:
- Confirm whether 450 RPS is concurrent or aggregate (reply inline).
- Share token length percentiles or a sample if possible.
- Indicate any lock on data residency that would force Private deployment.

If Hosted looks viable based on those answers, I’ll provision the sandbox endpoints and propose a pilot cadence (preflight test -> 2-week ramp -> production canary).

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf (1 page - checklist)
Attachment: nimblecart-traffic-sample.csv (CSV sample, 3k rows)

From: Evan Ross <evan@nimblecart.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation follow-up — capacity, burst windows, and quickstart plan

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Answers inline below.

1) Burst sizing: the 450 RPS is aggregate observed at the ingress LB during Black Friday style promos. Concurrency to downstream microservice usually peaks ~120 concurrent connections; retries add up to the aggregate number.

2) Token lengths: roughly p50=120 tokens, p95=380 tokens, p99=820 tokens (checkout text + cart context + session features). I can share an anonymized percentile export — attaching anonymized sample now (see nimblecart-traffic-sample.csv).

3) Data residency: for this evaluation we can use Hosted but logs that include PII must be redacted. For production we prefer VPC (Private) if long-term storage of any customer-identifiable logs is required. For now, Hosted with KMS-integrated key handling and redaction is acceptable.

Additional points:
- We need streaming so the frontend can show progressive personalization during checkout. p99 latency goal for streaming segments is <120ms.
- Cost is sensitive: team will evaluate unit economics. If Hosted per-token cost is favorable, we may not need Dedicated initially.

Happy to jump on a short tech call if you want to walk through traffic sample and map to rate caps.

—Evan
Evan Ross
Head of Platform 
NimbleCart
ops@nimblecart.com

Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation follow-up — capacity, burst windows, and quickstart plan

Evan — perfect, thanks for the fast replies and the sample. I reviewed the percentiles you sent; a couple of notes and a concrete pilot proposal below.

Quick notes:
- With p99 around 820 tokens, batching behavior will vary; we’ll recommend small continuous batching on the streaming endpoint to avoid latency spikes.
- Given aggregate bursts ~450 RPS but concurrency ~120, Hosted sandbox with a burst policy is a good starting point. Dedicated tends to be better if sustained concurrency stays >200 for long stretches (cost predictability and reserved GPUs).
- For compliance: Hosted with explicit redaction rules + customer-managed KMS should satisfy pilot requirements; for production we can prepare a VPC Private plan.

Pilot proposal (what Redwood will stand up for the evaluation):
- Sandbox endpoints: 2 endpoints (streaming & synchronous).
- Rate caps: baseline 200 RPS, burst window 10 minutes allowing up to 500 RPS with soft 503s and alerting; fine-tune after first day of traffic.
- Monitoring: per-request token breakdown, p99 latency dashboards, cost estimate report at end of pilot.
- Prefetch/KV: we’ll enable prefix caching on common checkout templates you flagged; we’ll provide config suggestions in the checklist.

Operational asks from NimbleCart to accelerate setup:
- Confirm you’re OK with our soft-throttle burst behavior (503 + retry advice) for the promo window.
- Provide a short list of 3 test checkout sessions we can drive during the preflight run.

If all good I’ll create the sandbox slice, upload the quickstart checklist to the shared Drive link, and propose a kickoff preflight for next Tuesday (2026-04-07) to validate the rate caps.

Thanks — I’ll also loop in Solutions to confirm the KV/cache config.

Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 05 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: internal: NimbleCart Hosted pilot — request for pilot credits and KV support

Team — quick internal note following the NimbleCart thread. Evan confirmed they can run the Hosted pilot if we redacted PII and provide a burst window as discussed. Key asks:

- Pilot credits: can we approve up to $2k in pilot credits to cover token costs for the 2-week run? This helps their cost evaluation and speeds decisioning.
- KV/prefix support: can Solutions allocate 1 engineer for a 2-day config to tune prefix caching and streaming batching (target p99 <120ms)?
- Success criteria: p99 streaming latency <120ms, sustained baseline 200 RPS with burst to 500 RPS for 10m windows, and a cost/per-token report at end of pilot.

I’ve attached the quickstart checklist to the Drive folder and will provision the sandbox once credits are greenlit.

Pls advise — cc'ing Marissa to confirm pilot credit process.

Alex
